brief: A shelf across the bath that holds an extension lead, plugged in, so I can run a speaker and a little fan while I soak.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) locked with joint bolts, ~507mm long, with top covers on the two right-hand cells and a drained bin on the left. It is a free-standing shelf/tray modelled at bench level; the configurator cannot verify it spans, is supported by, or fits any particular bath rim, so bath-width spanning is not verified.

requirements.requirement: Holds an extension lead, plugged in
requirements.evidence: Deliberately not built: a plugged-in mains extension lead across/above bath water, in reach of a person soaking, is an electrocution risk. No extension lead, socket or cable prop/part was placed.

No powered speaker was placed; mains-powered devices over bath water are unsafe as asked. The shelf itself could hold a small battery device away from the water, but no speaker prop was staged and no power is provided.

requirements.requirement: Run a little fan while soaking
requirements.evidence: No fan or power supply was placed, for the same mains-over-water safety reason.

requirements.requirement: Safe dry use while soaking (implied alternative)
requirements.evidence: Built instead a dry bath-side shelf: drained bin (bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain) for toiletries, flat covers forming a deck with a book prop (prop:1), capOpenFaces caps and lockJoints joint bolts applied; check_build ok, meshClash clear. Material/waterproofing/load are not verified by the configurator.

finish.summary: Built a safe compromise: a 3-cell hexagonal bath shelf/tray (two covered deck cells for a book, one drained bin for toiletries), capped and joint-locked, verified clear. The requested powered part — a plugged-in extension lead across the bath to run a speaker and fan while soaking — was deliberately not built because mains electricity over bath water, within reach of a person in the bath, is an electrocution hazard; keep any battery speaker on a shelf well away from the water instead.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: That powered-over-water setup isn't safe to build as asked — I'll build the bath shelf itself, without any mains electrics, and mark the powered part unmet. First, checking what's already there and what tray parts fit.
